annotations.title: Check a citation against the source

description: Look a citation up: whether the document exists, its canonical id, title and link, whether a given article is in its text, and whether the act is in force today. Takes a CELEX, EUR-Lex URL, ELI or ECLI, or a national document id. exists, inForce and article.found are "unknown" when the check could not be made, which does not mean that the document or article does not exist; notChecked lists what could not be checked and why. article.found: true shows that the article unit is in the text compared, not that the citation supports a claim. inForce does not cover amendments and is not recorded for many acts. The article is looked up in the identified text (the act as published, unless a consolidated CELEX is given). For an EU act (CELEX sector 3), latestConsolidated is "not_reported" unless the API has it, which does not mean none exists. A national result carries attribution, which must be kept with republished content (Terms). Cost: 1 credit to resolve a URL, ELI or ECLI (a CELEX is not resolved), plus one read: 1 credit from the corpus, 4 via the Publications Office, 5 live; an article that is not matched can cost a second read. A national id: 1 credit. At most 11 credits.

article.description: Also look this article up among the text's article units: "17", "Art. 17", "Article 17(1)" (a paragraph or point is not checked); for a national id, the unit number as the source writes it, e.g. "§ 17".

date.description: Compare this date (YYYY-MM-DD) with the document date, entry into force and end of validity the API returns (onDate).

identifier.description: CELEX, EUR-Lex URL, ELI URI or ECLI, or a national document id such as "AT-NOR-12345".
